title: How Fossils Are Formed
seo_title: Year 3 Science: How Fossils Are Formed Worksheets (Rock Layers and Mary Anning)
standard_text: Describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on fossils: how fossils form in rock, body and trace fossils, rock layers, what fossils tell us, and Mary Anning. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Trapped in rock for millions of years.
key_sub: Buried, pressed, turned to stone, then found.
body_html:
How to think about it

A fossil forms when a living thing is trapped in rock.

  • A plant or animal dies and is quickly buried in mud or sand. Soft parts rot away.
  • Layers build up and press down; minerals slowly replace the hard parts and turn them to stone.
  • In undisturbed rock, the lowest layers are the oldest. Mary Anning found famous fossils at Lyme Regis.
Example

After burial in mud, what next?

Soft parts rot

Answer: the soft parts rot away

Example

Which layer has the oldest fossils?

Layers build up on top

Answer: the bottom layer

Common mistakes

  • Thinking fossils form in a few years.
  • Thinking every animal becomes a fossil.
  • Thinking the top layer of rock is the oldest.

faq.a: A plant or animal dies and is quickly buried by mud or sand. The soft parts rot. Over millions of years the layers turn to rock and minerals replace the hard parts, making a stone copy.

faq.q: Which rock layer is the oldest?
faq.a: In rock that has not been disturbed, the bottom layer is the oldest, because new layers form on top.
